  (hxf : MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => inner ℝ x v * f x) (ProbabilityTheory.stdGaussian E))
  (hdf : MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => (fderiv ℝ f x) v) (ProbabilityTheory.stdGaussian E)) :

blind_reconstruction.text:
Let E be an arbitrary finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its compatible norm and Borel measurable structure. Write gamma_E for the measure defined by stdGaussian E. Concretely, if (e_k) is the standard orthonormal basis used in the definition, gamma_E is the pushforward of the finite product of real Gaussian laws gaussianReal(0,1) by (z_k) -> sum_k z_k e_k. The supplied density fixes each coordinate law as (2*pi)^(-1/2) exp(-t^2/2) dt: the mean is zero and the variance is one. Thus the Gaussian normalization is specified, not an unspecified scale. All integrals below are real Bochner/Lebesgue integrals over the whole E with respect to this same gamma_E.

For every scalar function f:E -> R and every fixed vector v in E, assume:
 (1) f is real Frechet differentiable at every x in E;
 (2) f is integrable with respect to gamma_E;
 (3) x -> <x,v> f(x) is integrable with respect to gamma_E;
 (4) x -> Df(x)[v] is integrable with respect to gamma_E.
Here Df(x):E ->L_R R is the Frechet derivative. The supplied Differentiable and DifferentiableAt definitions assert existence of an actual derivative at every point, and HasFDerivAt.fderiv identifies the literal fderiv_R f x with that derivative. Hence the right-hand integrand is the real linear derivative applied to the same fixed v.

Then
 integral_E <x,v> f(x) d gamma_E(x)
   = integral_E Df(x)[v] d gamma_E(x).

All three integrability conditions are explicit assumptions and are retained in this reconstruction. They mean almost-everywhere strong measurability and finite integral of the absolute value for these real functions. Differentiability holds everywhere, not only almost everywhere; continuity of the derivative, a C^1 hypothesis, compact support, boundary decay, and integrability of the entire derivative norm are not additional premises. The directional derivative integrability is for this chosen v only, not simultaneously for every direction. The vector v is arbitrary, with no nonzero or unit-norm restriction. There is no positive-dimension premise. There are no existential constants, error bounds, time horizons or limits. The conclusion is an equality of two finite real integrals, not a pointwise equality of the integrands or an equality of chosen quotient representatives.

import Mathlib.Probability.Distributions.Gaussian.Multivariate
import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.IsotropicGaussianDensity
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.LineDeriv.IntegrationByParts
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Calculus
import Mathlib.Tactic

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped InnerProductSpace ENNReal

noncomputable section

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.GaussianIntegrationByParts

section GaussianDensityHelpers
variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [CompleteSpace E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]

private def standardWeight (x : E) : ℝ :=
  ((Real.sqrt (2 * Real.pi))⁻¹) ^ Module.finrank ℝ E * Real.exp (-‖x‖^2 / 2)

private theorem standardWeight_pos (x : E) : 0 < standardWeight x := by
  dsimp [standardWeight]
  positivity

private theorem standardGaussian_density :
    stdGaussian E = (volume : Measure E).withDensity
      (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (standardWeight x)) := by
  have h := AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.IsotropicGaussianDensity.map_sqrt_smul_stdGaussian_eq_withDensity
    (E := E) 1 (by norm_num)
  simpa only [Real.sqrt_one, one_smul, Measure.map_id', mul_one,
    standardWeight] using h

private theorem standardGaussian_weighted_integral (g : E → ℝ) :
    (∫ x, g x ∂stdGaussian E) = ∫ x, standardWeight x * g x := by
  rw [standardGaussian_density]
  rw [integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul (by unfold standardWeight; fun_prop)
    (ae_of_all _ fun _ => ENNReal.ofReal_lt_top) g]
  apply integral_congr_ae
  filter_upwards with x
  simp only [ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (standardWeight_pos x).le, smul_eq_mul]

private theorem standardGaussian_weighted_integrable {g : E → ℝ}
    (hg : Integrable g (stdGaussian E)) :
    Integrable (fun x => standardWeight x * g x) (volume : Measure E) := by
  rw [standardGaussian_density] at hg
  have h := (integrable_withDensity_iff (by unfold standardWeight; fun_prop)
    (ae_of_all _ fun _ => ENNReal.ofReal_lt_top)).1 hg
  simpa only [ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (standardWeight_pos _).le, mul_comm] using h

private theorem standardWeight_hasFDerivAt (x : E) :
    HasFDerivAt (standardWeight : E → ℝ)
      (-(standardWeight x) • innerSL ℝ x) x := by
  let c : ℝ := ((Real.sqrt (2 * Real.pi))⁻¹) ^ Module.finrank ℝ E
  have h := (((hasFDerivAt_id x).norm_sq.const_mul (-1 / 2 : ℝ)).exp).const_mul c
  convert h using 1
  all_goals try rfl
  · funext y
    dsimp only [standardWeight, c, id]
    congr 1
    ring
  · ext v
    dsimp only [standardWeight, c, id]
    simp only [smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, innerSL_apply_apply,
      ContinuousLinearMap.comp_apply, ContinuousLinearMap.id_apply]
    have he : (-1 / 2 : ℝ) * ‖x‖^2 = -‖x‖^2 / 2 := by ring
    rw [he]
    ring

end GaussianDensityHelpers

theorem standard_gaussian_stein_of_integrable_fderiv
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    (f : E → ℝ) (v : E) (hf : Differentiable ℝ f)
    (hfi : Integrable f (stdGaussian E))
    (hxf : Integrable (fun x => ⟪x,v⟫_ℝ * f x) (stdGaussian E))
    (hdf : Integrable (fun x => fderiv ℝ f x v) (stdGaussian E)) :
    (∫ x, ⟪x,v⟫_ℝ * f x ∂stdGaussian E) =
      ∫ x, fderiv ℝ f x v ∂stdGaussian E := by
  let : CompleteSpace E := FiniteDimensional.complete ℝ E
  have hDw (x : E) : fderiv ℝ (standardWeight : E → ℝ) x v =
      -standardWeight x*inner ℝ x v := by
    rw [(standardWeight_hasFDerivAt x).fderiv]
    simp only [smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, innerSL_apply_apply]
  have hwp := standardGaussian_weighted_integrable hfi
  have hwdf := standardGaussian_weighted_integrable hdf
  have hwxf := standardGaussian_weighted_integrable hxf
  have hDwf : Integrable (fun x => fderiv ℝ (standardWeight : E → ℝ) x v*f x)
      (volume : Measure E) := by
    convert hwxf.neg using 1
    ext x
    rw [hDw]
    simp only [Pi.neg_apply]
    ring
  have hparts := integral_mul_fderiv_eq_neg_fderiv_mul_of_integrable hDwf hwdf hwp
    (fun x _ => (standardWeight_hasFDerivAt x).differentiableAt)
    (fun x _ => hf x)
  rw [standardGaussian_weighted_integral, standardGaussian_weighted_integral]
  calc
    (∫ x, standardWeight x*(inner ℝ x v*f x)) =
        -(∫ x, fderiv ℝ (standardWeight : E → ℝ) x v*f x) := by
      rw [← integral_neg]
      apply integral_congr_ae
      filter_upwards with x
      rw [hDw]
      ring
    _ = ∫ x, standardWeight x*fderiv ℝ f x v := hparts.symm

#print axioms standard_gaussian_stein_of_integrable_fderiv

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.GaussianIntegrationByParts

candidate_publication_context.statement: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel structure, and let \(\gamma=\operatorname{stdGaussian}(E)\). Fix a function \(f:E\to\mathbb R\) that is Fréchet differentiable everywhere and any direction \(v\in E\). Assume that each of \(f\), \(x\mapsto\langle x,v\rangle f(x)\), and \(x\mapsto Df(x)[v]\) is absolutely integrable under \(\gamma\). Then the weighted value and the directional derivative have the same Gaussian integral. No positive-dimension or unit-direction restriction is imposed.

formulae.label: Gaussian integration by parts on its integrable domain

assumptions: \(E\) is a real inner-product normed space of finite dimension, with its Borel measurable structure. Its completeness is derived.
\(\gamma\) is the actual centered Gaussian probability with identity covariance on \(E\).
\(f:E\to\mathbb R\) is Fréchet differentiable at every point, and \(v\in E\) is arbitrary, including zero.
\(\int_E|f|\,d\gamma<\infty\), \(\int_E|\langle x,v\rangle f(x)|\,d\gamma<\infty\), and \(\int_E|Df(x)[v]|\,d\gamma<\infty\). All three belong to this theorem’s stated domain.

steps.title: Transfer the stated integrability domain to Lebesgue measure
steps.text: Because \(\omega\) is positive, Gaussian integrability of a scalar function gives Lebesgue integrability after multiplication by \(\omega\). Apply this to the three assumed functions. The density derivative identifies the third weighted product, with its minus sign.
steps.formula: \omega f,\quad\omega Df[ v ],\quad D\omega[v]f=-\omega\langle x,v\rangle f\quad\text{are Lebesgue integrable}.
